title: Next Permutation
statement: Rearrange `nums` into the next lexicographically greater permutation. If none exists, rearrange it into the lowest order. Return the new order. Do it in place in the algorithm, even though the function returns the list.
hints: Find the rightmost index i where nums[i] < nums[i + 1]. That is the pivot that can still grow.
Swap it with the smallest value to its right that is still larger than it. That value is the rightmost successor.
Reverse the suffix after i so it becomes the smallest possible tail. If no pivot exists, reverse the whole array.

approaches.name: Pivot and reverse
approaches.explanation: One scan back, one scan for the successor, one reverse.

editorial: The suffix after the pivot is non-increasing, so it is the largest tail. The successor swap raises the pivot by the smallest possible amount, and reversing the suffix makes that tail the smallest possible. Together those steps produce the next permutation, and a fully non-increasing array wraps to the sorted order.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def next_permutation(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    i = len(nums) - 2
    while i >= 0 and nums[i] >= nums[i + 1]:
        i -= 1
    if i >= 0:
        j = len(nums) - 1
        while nums[j] <= nums[i]:
            j -= 1
        nums[i], nums[j] = nums[j], nums[i]
    left, right = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
    while left < right:
        nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return nums
